The Church fareth the better for her enemies petulancies and insolencies against her.

paragraphs.text: Or, The everlasting altitudes. Judea lay high; the Church is much higher.
paragraphs.anchor: Even the ancient high places.

paragraphs.text: Thus the Edomites triumphed before the victory. So did the Spaniards in 1588, and God heard them, {as Eze 35:13} for he is all-ear, all-eye, &c. He is jealous for his people, {Zec 1:14} and jealousy is quick sighted, quick conceited.
paragraphs.anchor: Are ours in possession.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Because and because; importing earnestness and heat of indignation. So Lev 26:43.
paragraphs.anchor: Because they have.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Ye are made to ascend upon the lip of the tongue, and upon the evil fame of the people. God takes it extreme ill that his people should be traduced and defamed; which yet hath been their lot in all ages; but he will not fail to vindicate them, and to avenge them.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye are taken up in the lips of talkers.

paragraphs.text: For men there were hardly any left, or not very fit to be dealt with. See Eze 36:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore thus saith the Lord God to the mountains.

paragraphs.text: To those man eaters, {Eze 36:3} qui diruerunt et devoraverunt, who did eat up God’s people as they ate bread, {Psa 14:4} making themselves merry with their misery.
paragraphs.anchor: Which became a prey.

paragraphs.text: Jealousy is hot as hell; {Son 8:6} it is implacable, {Pro 6:34-35} and very vindictive. See Zec 1:14. {See Trapp on "Zec 1:14"} Here God swears he will be even with these Edomites.
paragraphs.anchor: Surely in the fire of my jealousy.

paragraphs.text: This the Lord hath never done with, so ill be took it.
paragraphs.anchor: Which have appointed my land.

paragraphs.text: To those lifeless creatures he directeth his speech, to show that every creature groaneth and waiteth for the redemption of our bodies. It fareth the better also in this life present, for the elect’s sake, as it was once cursed for man’s sin, and hath lain bedridden, as it were, ever since.
paragraphs.anchor: Say unto the mountains and to the hills.

paragraphs.text: This the Lord could not bear with any patience.
paragraphs.anchor: Because ye have borne the shame of the heathen.

paragraphs.text: Sworn solemnly. Men, when they swear, do so as taking God to witness. Three fingers they do often lift up, and hold down two, to signify, saith Lavater, that God, who is three in one, hath prepared a place in heaven for such as swear rightly, but will thrust down to hell those that forswear themselves.
paragraphs.anchor: I have lifted up mine hand.

paragraphs.text: They shall be paid home in their own coin, be overshot in their own bow, be covered with their own confusion.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall bear their shame.

paragraphs.text: Reflourish and fructify; the Christian churches (those spiritual mountains) shall especially. {Rev 22:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Ye shall shoot forth your branches.

paragraphs.text: To come home out of captivity, or to return to God by repentance. The fall of Antichrist cannot be far off.
paragraphs.anchor: For they are at hand to come.

paragraphs.text: Or, I come to you, and I come with a cornucopia in mine hand.
paragraphs.anchor: For, behold, I am for you.

paragraphs.text: The Israel of God in the kingdom of the Messiah, totum totum, quantum quantum, not one of them shall be missing.
paragraphs.anchor: All the house of Israel, even all of it.

paragraphs.text: This must necessarily be understood of spiritual blessings by Christ; for temporals, they never had the like to those in the days of Joshua, David, Solomon, Hezekiah, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And will do better unto you.

paragraphs.text: Yea, a type and pledge of that heavenly inheritance. {1Pe 1:4 Rev 21:1-10; Rev 21:22-27; Rev 22:1-5}
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt be their inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Provoke God to bereave them.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them.

paragraphs.text: {a} scil., By pestilence, famine, sword, evil beasts: thou art an unlucky land, an unblest country, feral and fatal to thine inhabitants. Hesiod saith the like of his country Ascre; and another {b} of St David’s in Wales, that it is a place neither pleasant, fertile, nor safe. Strabo saith the like of Judea, but with a despiteful mind. {as Eze 36:5} Those malevolent spies said no less. {Num 13:32}
paragraphs.anchor: Thou land devourest up men

paragraphs.text: {a} Terra abortiens populos.
{b} Girald., Cambrens.
Either by consuming them, or spuing them out. {as Lev 18:28; Lev 20:22; Lev 26:20; Lev 26:22} See what is said of heaven, Rev 22:3-5.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither bereave thy nations any more.

paragraphs.text: I will cut off all occasions, and remove all such stumblingblocks as whereat the nations dash and split themselves.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither will I cause men to hear.

paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the word.

paragraphs.text: Ubique Scriptura vindicat gloriam Dei, maxime autem hoc loco. {a} This place of Scripture doth singularly set forth the glory of God’s grace, while it showeth that man’s destruction is wholly of himself, his help only of God.

These two gross sins are instanced, viz., murder and idolatry, lest they should plead, as in Jer 2:35, "I have not sinned"; or as in Hos 12:8, "In all my works they shall find none iniquity in me; that were sin."
paragraphs.anchor: For the blood which they had shed.

paragraphs.text: Whose idols they had worshipped, and whose manners they had imitated.
paragraphs.anchor: And I scattered them among the heathen.

paragraphs.text: And these are the fruits of their religion. Are these the holy people? &c. Lactantius {a} complaineth of his times, that God’s truth was evil spoken of by the heathen, because Christians lived loosely and lewdly. Whereupon Erasmus {b} crieth out, O rem miseram! Oh, lamentable! Even in those purer times the piety of Christians was so much abated, that the gospel was therefore evil spoken of, for the evil lives of many that professed it. What marvel then, saith he, that Turks cry out upon us? that the banks of blasphemy are broken down in persons disaffected to the power of godliness?
paragraphs.anchor: These are the people of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lactant., de Opific. Dei; Proaem.
{b} Erasm. in Lactant.

So he hath still, or else it would be wide enough with us. Some render it, I spared, or tendered, mine holy name; and, to free it from those imputations, I freely forgave my people, and re-established them.
paragraphs.anchor: But I had pity for my holy name.

paragraphs.text: To do good without respect of desert is royal, yea, it is divine.
paragraphs.anchor: I do not this for your sakes.

paragraphs.text: But for mine own holy name’s sake.] God maketh our utter unworthiness a foil to set forth the freeness of his love, in making us worthy whom he found not so.

I will recover my reputation among the heathen, by declaring my justice in your punishment, and my mercy in your restoration. God, as he is moved by his own grace to do his people good, so he aimeth therein at his own glory.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will sanctify my great name.

paragraphs.text: I will effectually call you out of darkness into my marvellous light, and cull you out from this wicked world. And this is the first thing that God here promiseth to his covenanters. More than this, he promiseth them in the following verses justification, sanctification, and preservation, or provision of temporal blessings, that nothing may be wanting to them that may make them happy. We should be often counting of this coin, telling of this treasure.
paragraphs.anchor: For I will take you, &c.

paragraphs.text: He alludeth to the legal purifications, especially that made by the ashes of a red cow mixed with running water, wherewith the people were sprinkled, and so cleansed from legal defilement. {Num 19:17-19} Semblably the saints, sprinkled with Christ’s blood from an evil conscience by the hyssop bunch of faith, and so washed with clean water {Heb 10:22} in baptism, the saving virtue whereof is permanent, {1Pe 3:21} are justified and sanctified. {1Co 6:11} This blessed sprinkling David prayeth for. {Psa 51:2} The Baptist also, and others, sprinkled those whom they baptized, both to answer the types of the law and this prediction of the prophet, understood by Jerome {a} of baptism, which is a visible sign and seal of our being washed from the filth of sin by the merit and Spirit of Jesus Christ. {Tit 3:5}
paragraphs.anchor: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you.

paragraphs.text: {a} Epist. 83.

For the old heart will never hold out the hardship of holiness; the old fabric must be taken down, and a new set up. See Eze 11:19. A "new man" both in constitution and conversation one must be, or else he is no man in Christ. {2Co 5:17}
paragraphs.anchor: A new heart also will I give you.

paragraphs.text: The natural heart, which is hard and refractory, "to every good work reprobate." Hard is that which resisteth the touch. The old heart is inflexible to God’s Spirit, insensible of his word and judgments, and impenetrable to his grace. Where, then, is man’s freewill? Garriant illi, nos credamus; { a} there is no such thing, believe it. Nature is wholly stony: it is God alone that "of these stones raiseth up children to Abraham."
paragraphs.anchor: And I will taks away the stony heart.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Tractable, and capable of divine impressions, ready to every good work. {Tit 3:1}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will give you an heart of flesh

paragraphs.text: {a} Augustine.
Qui mulcendo et molliendo. Who, by melting and mollifying your hard hearts, shall bring you to a better obedience.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will put my Spirit within you.

paragraphs.text: Lex iubet, gratia iuvat. God undertaketh for himself and his people too, viz., to work in them what he requireth of them. Therefore it is an "everlasting covenant, ordered in all things"; and the fruits of it are "sure mercies," "compassions that fail not," &c. See on Eze 11:20.
paragraphs.anchor: And cause you to walk in my statutes.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In Judea, or rather in the Church, {a} which began in Judea, saith the Jesuit well The Church of Rome, then, is not the mother Church; no, though we take it in its primitive purity.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall dwell in the land

paragraphs.text: {a} A Lapide.

This is often promised, because not easily believed. No article of our creed is so much opposed by Satan, as that of the forgiveness of sin by Christ’s merits, which is the very life and soul of a Church. All the former articles of the creed are perfected in this, and all the following articles are effects thereof: hold it fast, therefore.
paragraphs.anchor: I will also save you from all your uncleannesses.

paragraphs.text: I have it at my call, and a mandamus from me will do it at any time. See Hos 2:21-22. {See Trapp on "Hos 2:21"} {See Trapp on "Hos 2:22"}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will call for the corn.

paragraphs.text: Which comes also at God Almighty’s call. {Psa 105:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And lay no famine.

paragraphs.text: The heathen were often twitting God’s people with their outward wants and crosses, as if caused by their religion. So the persecutors did by the primitive Christians, and so the Papists still deal with the New Gospellers, as they scornfully call the Reformed Churches.
paragraphs.anchor: That ye shall receive no more reproach.

paragraphs.text: The goodness of God shall lead you to repentance; so many mercies heaped upon so undeserving, nay, so illdeserving creatures, shall bring you to a deep detestation of your iniquities.
paragraphs.anchor: Then shall ye remember.

paragraphs.text: There are some things, saith one, that we can hardly forget, viz., our sorrows and our pleasures, as Esau; some things we can hardly remember, as our faults and our friends, as Joseph’s butler. Augustine was famous, saith another for two of his works: his Retractions, which are the confessions of his errors; and his Confessions, which are the retractions of his life. See Eze 20:43.
paragraphs.anchor: Your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good.

paragraphs.text: Or, Ye shall look upon yourselves as worthy to be destroyed. Or, Ye shall scold within yourselves against your iniquities. Litigabitis intra vos contra flagitia vestra.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall loathe yourselves.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 36:22.
paragraphs.anchor: Not for your sakes.

paragraphs.text: Abashed and abased, as was Ezra, {Ezr 9:6} Ephraim, {Jer 31:19} the publican. {Luk 18:13}
paragraphs.anchor: Be ashamed.

paragraphs.anchor: And the desolate land shall be tilled.

paragraphs.text: Such a change can God soon make for worse or better. Fear him therefore; fear the Lord and his goodness. {Hos 3:5}
paragraphs.anchor: This land.

paragraphs.text: Haec iam ex parte fata sunt, saith Oecolampadius. This day is this scripture fulfilled in our eyes: the ruined churches are rebuilt, and the matter well amended by this blessed Reformation, and Rome knows it.
paragraphs.anchor: Then the heathen.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Though I have promised my people all these boons, yet I look they should put my promises in suite, by praying them over. Prayer is an indispensable duty, and must not on any pretence whatsoever be neglected.
paragraphs.anchor: I will yet for this be inquired of

paragraphs.text: Plenty of men and store of children is a great blessing of God. Yet some are ready to say of them, as that rustic did of his afflictions, when he was told they were God’s love tokens, Ah quam velim alios amare, non me. Oh how I wish to love others, not myself. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: I will increase them with men like a flock.

paragraphs.text: {a} Luther.
The sheep that come up for sacrifice, at the passover especially; so will I multiply the sheep of Christ, the true shepherd.
paragraphs.anchor: As the holy flock.
